articles.title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
articles.description: Nvidia’s new SoC is available in Windows laptops from six different manufacturers. We’ve collectively tested four of them so far. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Nvidia's RTX Spark N1X processor is finally here, and we've been collectively testing a small fortune's worth of powerful laptops sporting this new "superchip." RTX Spark is designed to be a high-performing Arm-based SoC for laptops and small desktop computers, rivaling the best from Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. It has loads of cores, Nvidia RTX Blackwell graphics, and enough power and unified memory to run sizable local AI models. The flagship placement is inside Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with a staggering 128GB of unified memory, which our own Tom Warren fully reviewed. articles.title: Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For Its Cash?
articles.description: Over the last twelve months, Qualcomm (QCOM) generated free cash flow equal to 5.5% of its market value. That outpaces the 4.4% yield for the median S&P 500 company. A yield above the median can mean a business that is either on sale or expected to shrink. Qualcomm's revenue fell in each of its last two quarters. So is that cash the sign of a business on sale, or of one that is shrinking.
